unharnessed.meaning: Every instruction survives, numbers intact: "It's 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter in the sun", "Plan your day so you're not walking between 10am and 4pm", "cotton's great in the desert!", the rangers' snack list.
unharnessed.sense: Terms carry the sense: "you mightn't twig how much fluid you're losing", "not running out of puff" for avoiding fatigue, "Have a spell somewhere near shade", "staying out of strife" for avoiding hazards, "keep the tank full".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Australian advice voice: "quick smart", "chuck in their day packs", "finish up late arvo", "the temperature can go through the roof". The heading keeps US "Stay Hydrated and Energized".
unharnessed.register: Level 3: the leaflet is retold in plain Aussie speech without piling on; "a simple but bloody effective way" is a single dad-level swear, within the brief.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the upbeat, practical park-service tone, exclamations and all: "tasty tucker that's ready for the track!", "so don't skip this simple but vital way to cool down!"
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Get going before sunrise and finish up late arvo."
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("twig", "chuck", "tucker", "puff", "spell", "strife", "through the roof"), with "walk"/"walking" repeated as the stock replacement for hike.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the hike-smart guidance: hydration, salty snacks, timing, staying wet: "One of the best ways to keep your body temperature in check ... is to stay sopping wet."

engine.meaning: Nearly the original word for word, so nothing is lost: "Sun temperatures are 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter than posted shade temperatures."
engine.sense: The few swaps mostly fit ("a late arvo finish", "bushwalkers"), but "cotton is ripper in the desert!" stretches 'great' (useful) into a cheer.
engine.authenticity: What little Aussie there is sits on unchanged US prose: "offers unique challenges due to the combination of ambient temperature, elevation", "Stay Hydrated and Energized", "stay cool and energized", "the timing of their hike".
engine.register: Largely untranslated: apart from "Bushwalking", "arvo" and "ripper", it is the original leaflet, far below level 3.
engine.tone: The original's tone is intact because the text is: "tasty and trail-ready fuel for the journey!"
engine.flow: Reads as the original does, but the swaps clash: "Experienced desert bushwalkers know that the timing of their hike".
engine.variety: Only three Aussie items, "bushwalking" repeated: "Bushwalking in the Grand Canyon", "not bushwalking between", "while bushwalking".
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, being nearly the original.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points kept, numbers intact: "It's 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter in the sun", "not walking between the hours of 10am and 4pm", the snack list, "cotton is ripper in the desert!".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Fits throughout: "hard yakka" for demanding, "you won't get buggered" for fatigue, "peckish", "staying out of strife", "keep the engine running", "sit out the worst of the heat".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian ranger: "a different beast", "your sweat dries off that quick you mightn't even realise", "chuck in their daypacks", "finish up late in the arvo".
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3: an easy Aussie retelling; "buggered" is a dad-level word within the brief.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the friendly, practical leaflet tone: "Tasty tucker, and ready for the track!" "And remember, staying soaking wet isn't just about feeling better."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth spoken advice; one clunky join: "you'll have a heaps better time out on the tracks, and it'll be worth the effort".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the Grand Canyon hike-smart page, every section in place: "KEEP YOURSELF SOAKING WET TO STAY COOL."

yarn-troppo.meaning: All instructions survive, but it adds claims: "Now this is the trick I reckon most people miss.", "cooler and fresher than you'd ever expect", "it might just save your bacon", "Don't be one of them."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "hard yakka", "salty snacks are the go", "won't end up buggered", "steering clear of heat exhaustion", "Simple as".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural Aussie voice ("salty snacks are the go", "Simple as, and it works a treat"), but the frame lines are stock: "Now, this one's a ripper, and it might just save your bacon." "Can't argue with that!"
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: a yarn frame and asides on every section ("Here's the thing.", "But here's the catch.", "And here's a number to think about."). No swearing past dad.
yarn-troppo.tone: The leaflet's upbeat practicality stays, but the showman patter ("It's like walking into an oven, a bit at a time.") makes it more of a pitch than a safety page.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well, though the repeated lead-ins stack: "Here's the thing.", "But here's the catch.", "Now this is the trick".
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range of slang: "save your bacon", "no stroll down the beach", "the go", "hard yakka", "peckish", "buggered", "strife", "works a treat".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the original, but the added framing ("Now, this one's a ripper") turns the leaflet into a fireside talk.

yarn-deadset.meaning: Complete and accurate: "Temperatures in the sun are 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter than the posted shade temperatures", "not walking between the hours of 10am and 4pm".
yarn-deadset.sense: Mostly exact ("hard yakka", "not getting buggered", "staying out of strife"), but "a simple but handy way to stay cool" weakens the original's 'effective'.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural where it uses Aussie: "chuck in their daypacks", "dodge the worst of the heat", "late in the arvo"; some sentences stay close to the leaflet: "By staying on top of your water, your tucker and your rest, you'll help make your time".
yarn-deadset.register: Level 3: the leaflet in a light-to-moderate Aussie voice, with dad-level "buggered".
yarn-deadset.tone: Keeps the friendly, practical tone with its exclamations: "tasty tucker that's ready for the track!"
yarn-deadset.flow: Mostly smooth, with a repeat: "eat enough to keep your body going. Having snacks regularly ... will help keep you going."
yarn-deadset.variety: Reasonable range ("tucker", "hard yakka", "buggered", "strife", "ripper"), "tucker" leaned on: "your water and your tucker", "water and tucker right", "your tucker and your rest".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original page, sections intact.

summaries.unharnessed: A clean, natural level-3 retelling that keeps every instruction and the leaflet's upbeat tone.
summaries.engine: Essentially the original with a few words swapped; accurate but almost no Aussie.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: The most natural and varied version: complete, idiomatic, and true to the leaflet's tone.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Vivid and idiomatic, but told as a yarn with added framing and claims, heavier than the brief.
summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful, lightly Aussie version; a little flatter and more repetitive than the best.
